facts.text: ASAM OSI (Open Simulation Interface) is a standard set of messages connecting an environment model, a sensor model and the function under test during simulation; ASAM is the industry association that publishes it.
facts.quote: ASAM OSI is a standard set of messages that lets an environment model, a sensor model and the function under test talk to each other during a simulation, and ASAM is the industry association that publishes it.

facts.text: ASAM OSI standardizes messages for ground truth (the true positions of everything), sensor views, sensor data and detected objects, each with time stamps.
facts.quote: OSI (Open Simulation Interface) standardizes the shape of those messages: ground truth (the true positions of everything), sensor views, sensor data and detected objects, each with time stamps.

facts.text: A sensor model written to ASAM OSI can move from one simulator to another.
facts.quote: A sensor model written to OSI can move from one simulator to another

facts.text: ASAM OSI allows a supplier to deliver a sensor model as a sealed package that hides the supplier's intellectual property.
facts.quote: a supplier can deliver its model as a sealed package that hides its intellectual property [Chapters 6, 7].

facts.text: ASAM (Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems) is a nonprofit association based in Germany whose members include vehicle manufacturers, suppliers and tool vendors.
facts.quote: ASAM (Association for Standardization of Automation and Measuring Systems) is a nonprofit association, based in Germany, of vehicle manufacturers, suppliers and tool vendors.

facts.text: Besides OSI, ASAM publishes the OpenX scene and scenario formats and OpenMATERIAL 3D.
facts.quote: Besides OSI it publishes the OpenX scene and scenario formats and OpenMATERIAL 3D [Chapters 5, 9, 11].

facts.text: ASAM's ecosystem grew up around road vehicles, but the booklet rates OSI and the model-coupling standard FMI (Functional Mock-up Interface) as domain-neutral and transferring well to off-road work.
facts.quote: Its ecosystem grew up around road vehicles, but the booklet rates OSI, like the model-coupling standard FMI (Functional Mock-up Interface), as domain-neutral and transferring well to off-road work [Chapter 9].

facts.text: ASAM states that no standardized metrics exist to judge sensor-simulation quality.
facts.quote: ASAM's own statement that "no standardized metrics exist" to judge sensor-simulation quality

facts.text: The project to define standardized sensor-simulation quality metrics was still at proposal stage in September 2025.
facts.quote: the project to define them was still at proposal stage in September 2025

facts.text: A project to extend ASAM OSI for high-fidelity sensor simulation runs from April 2025 to March 2027.
facts.quote: a project to extend OSI for high-fidelity sensor simulation runs from April 2025 to March 2027 [Chapters 7, 11].

facts.text: The booklet recommends fixing the semantic contract early, before hardware: define what a detected object, a warning state and a brake request mean independently of any sensor supplier. ASAM OSI shows the pattern for this contract.
facts.quote: Fixing the semantic contract early (what a "detected object", a warning state and a brake request mean, independent of any sensor supplier) is one of the booklet's pre-hardware steps, and OSI shows the pattern

facts.text: The brake request in the booklet's semantic contract is anchored by the J1939 interface of ISO/TS 21815-2.
facts.quote: the brake request itself is anchored by the J1939 interface of ISO/TS 21815-2 [Chapter 7].
